title: CORP: Closed-Form One-shot Representation-Preserving Structured Pruning for Transformers
claim: Removing structured components is offset by compensation that reconstructs their contribution from retained components, folded into remaining weights.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; dashed zoom-in callouts, hatched pruned blocks
description: Two panels show how pruning and compensation work inside a transformer. Panel (a), Attention Head Dimension Pruning, shows matrix products: input X times the query weight WQ, and WK^T times X^T. Dashed rounded callouts zoom into the Q and K projection matrices. Below them are the Query matrix, the Key^T matrix and a green attention-map grid. Solid blocks are sustained channels. Cross-hatched blocks are pruned channels. Red arrows labeled Ranking show the order in which channels are scored. Green curved arrows labeled Compensation point from the pruned blocks back to the retained ones. Panel (b), MLP Channel Pruning, runs left to right: input feature, W1, hidden feature, W2 and output feature. Purple, orange and pink blocks are partly hatched. A legend under each panel explains Sustain, Prune, Ranking and Compensation.
caption: Illustration of CORP. Pruning removes structured components, while CORP reconstructs the missing contribution using closed-form compensation folded into the remaining weights. (a) Attention head dimension pruning removes channel dimensions in the query and key projections. (b) MLP structured pruning removes entire hidden dimensions between the two linear layers.
abstract: Transformers achieve strong accuracy but incur high compute and memory cost. Structured pruning reduces inference cost, but most methods rely on retraining or multi-stage optimization, which limits post-training deployment. We propose CORP, a closed-form one-shot structured pruning method that removes MLP dimensions and attention substructures using only unlabeled calibration data without gradients or fine-tuning. CORP formulates structured pruning as a representation recovery problem. It models removed components as affine functions of retained components and derives closed-form ridge regression solutions that fold compensation into model weights. This minimizes a layer-local affine/logit reconstruction objective under the calibration distribution. Experiments on ImageNet with DeiT reveal strong redundancy in both MLP and attention representations. With CORP, models retain high accuracy under aggressive sparsity. On DeiT-Huge, CORP achieves 83.24% Top-1 accuracy after pruning 50% of both MLP and attention structures.
